_comment: EVERY GAP THIS GATE IS ALLOWED TO HAVE, NAMED. A gap is a row validate.py could not decide:
it is recorded SKIP with a reason, printed as DID NOT VERIFY, and removed from the owed set so
the verdict can still judge the rows that exist. That removal is exactly how a gap hides — an
id that stops being checked stops being counted, and a run with one fewer thing verified reads
the same green as a run with one more. So the gaps are declared HERE, and run.sh refuses any
run whose gaps are not the ones this file names, in no greater number than it names.
`expected` is the most SKIP rows a run may produce. `accepted` names them: one entry per gap,
`cells` a regex over the ledger id (`<cell-id>#request` / `#response`, same convention as
testing/shadow-oracle/accepted-gaps.json), plus an `owner` and a `rationale`. An entry missing
any of the three is refused — a gap with no owner is a gap nobody is fixing. A SKIP row whose
own reason is empty is refused too: named means named, on the row.
FEWER gaps than declared is never red — a gap that closed is what this file exists to drive
towards — but it is printed with the instruction to lower `expected`, so the floor only ever
moves down. MORE, or one this file does not name, is red.
Every entry today is a cell testing/shadow-oracle/record.sh could not record at all (its own
ledger says UNSUPPORTED), so there is no wire for this gate to judge. They are the recorder's
to close, not this rig's; when a fixture lands, the cell records, the rows go PASS or FAIL on
their merits, and the entry and the count come off.

accepted.rationale: The mock upstream cannot yet fail PART WAY THROUGH a stream — N good events, then an in-band error event — so the recorder reports UNSUPPORTED for this outcome in all six ingress dialects and there is no recorded wire to judge. 12 rows: 6 dialects x {request, response}.

A request that puts a `cachePoint` before a native `document` block — a wire slot that yields no IR block, ahead of one that does — has no fixture in the tree, so the recorder reports UNSUPPORTED and records nothing.

An answer carrying a URL citation — the Responses annotation the published UrlCitationBody flattens onto the annotation object — has no fixture in the tree, so the recorder reports UNSUPPORTED and records nothing.
